Convert lines to a landscape network (LSN)

Source: R/lines_to_lsn.R
lines_to_lsn.Rd

Convert an sf object containing features with LINESTRING geometry to a landscape network (LSN), which is a topological data model of streams/rivers represented as a directional graph embedded in 2-D geographic space. Relationship tables are created and topological relationships are checked.

lines_to_lsn(
  streams,
  lsn_path,
  check_topology = TRUE,
  snap_tolerance,
  topo_tolerance,
  remove_ZM = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  use_parallel = NULL,
  no_cores = NULL
)

Arguments

streams

An sf object with LINESTRING geometry representing streams.

lsn_path

Pathname to a directory in character format specifying where to store the outputs. The directory will be created if it does not already exist.

check_topology

Logical. If TRUE, the edges will be checked for topological errors and potential node errors will be flagged in an output file called node_errors.gpkg. Defaults to TRUE.

snap_tolerance

Distance in map units >= 0. Required; there is no default. Two nodes separated by a distance less than or equal to snap_tolerance are assumed to be connected. Use 0 to connect only line end nodes with identical coordinates.

topo_tolerance

Distance in map units. Required when check_topology = TRUE, and ignored otherwise. Two nodes on the network separated by a distance less than or equal to topo_tolerance are flagged as potential topological errors in the network. Must be greater than snap_tolerance (and therefore > 0) when check_topology = TRUE.

remove_ZM

Logical. If TRUE, Z and M dimensions are removed from streams, if they exist. If FALSE and streams has Z and/or M dimensions, the function stops with an error. Default is FALSE.

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE, output files will overwrite existing files with the same names, and a node_errors.gpkg file from an earlier run is deleted. Default is FALSE.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, messages describing function progress will be printed to the console. Default is TRUE.

use_parallel

Deprecated and ignored. Parallel processing is no longer needed. Supplying it gives a warning.

no_cores

Deprecated and ignored. Parallel processing is no longer needed. Supplying it gives a warning.

Value

An sf object representing edges in the LSN. The LSN, including edges.gpkg, nodes.gpkg, noderelationships.csv, and relationships.csv files, are saved locally to a directory defined by lsn_path. If check_topology = TRUE and topological errors are identified, then node_errors.gpkg is also saved to lsn_path.

Details

lines_to_lsn converts an sf object representing streams to a landscape network (LSN), which is a directional graph used to represent the topological and geographic relationships between line features, along with additional attribute information. streams must have LINESTRING geometry and a projected coordinate system, rather than geographic coordinate system (i.e. not Longitude and Latitude).

The LSN is saved to a local directory defined by lsn_path and has four components:

  • nodes.gpkg: A GeoPackage of features with POINT geometry representing topologic breaks in the stream network. A column named nodecat specifies the type of node (e.g. pseudonodes, confluences, stream sources, or stream outlets). A column containing a unique node identifier, pointid, is also included.

  • edges.gpkg: A GeoPackage of features with LINESTRING geometry representing flow paths (i.e. line features) from node to node. A new column named rid is added that contains a unique identifier for each line feature.

  • noderelationships.csv: a table describing the relationship between the nodes and their associated edges, as well as directionality in the LSN. The table contains three columns: the rid (for each edge), fromnode (pointid for the upstream node of each edge), and tonode (pointid for the downstream node of each edge). Directionality is defined based on the digitized direction of the line features.

  • relationships.csv: a table representing the downstream flow path from edge to edge. The table contains two columns: fromedge (upstream edge) and toedge (downstream edge).

Line end nodes separated by a Euclidean distance <= snap_tolerance are snapped together into a single node, and nodes, noderelationships.csv and relationships.csv are all built from this rule. Snapping is transitive: if end node A is within snap_tolerance of end node B, and B is within snap_tolerance of end node C, then A, B and C are snapped even if A and C are further apart. The upstream and downstream end nodes of the same line feature are never snapped into one node. The node takes the coordinates of the first line end node assigned to it.

Topological errors are common in spatial data and must be corrected to ensure the LSN accurately represents direction and connectivity within the stream network. When check_topology = TRUE, the edges are checked for topological errors and potential errors are saved to lsn_path in an output file called node_errors.gpkg. In addition to the pointid, node_errors.gpkg contains a column containing the node category (nodecat), which like nodes.gpkg can take on values of Pseudonode, Confluence, Source, or Outlet. Another column (error) defines the potential error type and can take on values of:

  • Complex Confluence: three or more edges flow into the node.

  • Converging Node: two edges flow into the node and none flow out.

  • Dangling Node: an outlet within topo_tolerance of an edge in a different network.

  • Downstream Divergence: two or more edges flow out of the node.

  • Intersection Without Node: two edges cross without a node. A crossing within snap_tolerance of a node that both edges flow into or out of is not reported.

  • Confluence Without Node: an edge end node touches another edge somewhere other than the end node (e.g. forms a T junction where the other edge is not split).

  • Network Without Outlet: the node is part of a loop of edges with no outlet (e.g. edges digitised in a circle, with or without edges flowing into it). Every node on the loop is reported.

  • Self-loop: the upstream and downstream end nodes of a line feature have identical coordinates. The line feature is not included in relationships.csv.

  • Chained Node: the node contains line end nodes more than snap_tolerance apart. Because snapping is transitive, this happens when end nodes are linked by a chain of end nodes, each within snap_tolerance of the next.

  • Unsnapped Node: a line end node was <= snap_tolerance from another end node and was not snapped to it. This typically occurs when snapping would result in a line feature's to and from nodes being combined into one node (e.g. a line end node close to both end nodes of a short line).

Two additional columns are added to node_errors.gpkg containing the rids of the edges flowing into (up_rid) and out of (down_rid) each node, in comma separated text format (e.g. "4, 7"). This allows the user to visually check flow relationships at each potential error more quickly. Note that up_rid is NA for a node without edges that flow in (e.g. a Source) and down_rid is NA for a node without edges flowing out (e.g. an Outlet). Both are NA for Intersection Without Node errors, along with pointid and nodecat, because these do not coincide with topological breaks in the edges. A numeric column (node_width) gives the largest distance, in map units, between two line end nodes in each Chained Node, so the widest can be checked first. Note that node_width is NA for all other error types.

There is no guarantee that all topological errors will be identified and included in node_errors.gpkg. Therefore, potential errors and node classes found in node_errors.gpkg and nodes.gpkg must be checked and topological errors in streams corrected before rebuilding the LSN using lines_to_lsn(). This process is iterative and must continue until the LSN is free of topological errors. A node_errors.gpkg file is not produced if no obvious errors are identified.

The arguments snap_tolerance and topo_tolerance are both provided in map units and neither has a default. snap_tolerance must always be provided and must be >= 0. When check_topology = TRUE, topo_tolerance must also be provided and must be greater than snap_tolerance. It is generally a good idea to set the snap_tolerance to a distance shorter than the smallest line segment length. It should also be relatively small compared to the distance specified in the topo_tolerance argument. Nodes separated by a Euclidean distance <= snap_tolerance are assumed to be connected and are snapped together. When snap_tolerance < distance <= topo_tolerance, nodes are flagged as potential errors. If snap_tolerance is too large, end nodes that should remain separate will be snapped together in error. If topo_tolerance is too large, more false errors will be flagged in node_errors.gpkg.

WARNING: A warning is given if the length of any line feature in streams is <= snap_tolerance, because snapping near that line feature may not give the intended connections. Use st_length to obtain and check the minimum length of the line features prior to running lines_to_lsn. When check_topology = FALSE, a warning is also given if any line end nodes within snap_tolerance of another line end node were not snapped. This typically occurs when snapping would put both end nodes of a line feature into one node. If this warning is returned, re-run lines_to_lsn with check_topology = TRUE to locate these nodes. Similarly, when check_topology = FALSE, a warning is given if any snapped nodes include Chained Nodes that were more than snap_tolerance apart because of transitive snapping. Again, use check_topology = TRUE to locate and check these nodes.
